problem: Existing outdoor VLN models (Touchdown, map2seq) predict actions from panorama and instruction features only, ignoring individual objects and scene text in the environment, and learn data bias. Most failures come from turning or stopping at the wrong place.
motivation: Humans navigate unfamiliar outdoor places by using identifiable objects and store names as landmarks, which supports accurate turns and stops. The authors' preliminary analysis found that most failures of prior models were wrong turns or wrong stops, so grounding the agent in on-the-route objects and scene text should address this.
key_idea: Add an Object-Attention VLN (OAVLN) model that makes the agent attend to relevant on-the-route objects and scene text during training, so it grounds instruction landmarks in the environment.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so the ablations are not visible. The abstract's claim is that landmark-level object and text grounding reduces turn and stop errors, which are the dominant failure modes of panorama-only outdoor VLN.
method: Object-Attention VLN (OAVLN): an outdoor VLN model that adds object-level features to the panorama and instruction features used for action prediction.
Object attention: the agent is trained to focus on objects relevant to the instruction, such as landmarks and store names.
Scene text use: text detected in the scene (for example store names) serves as reference landmarks. Details are not given in the abstract.
